summary: A life told looking back ties an early day to what came after it: the office the writer went on to hold, the bills the writer went on to bring, the years between.
realLife: People who tell their own past connect an earlier event to later parts of their life, and that link is a large part of how an event comes to mean something in the telling. A diary entry kept in the moment cannot say it; a life told afterward can.
sources: Differences Between Subclinical Ruminators and Reflectors in Narrating Autobiographical Memories: Innovative Moments and Autobiographical Reasoning (PubMed Central): https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7982801/
inGame: journal-later.ts reads the person's later office terms and sponsored bills (laterRecordsOf, #10579); the evening entry carries the slots once journal-evening.ts makes the call.

turns.what: The writer never holds office or brings a bill, so the entry stays what it was: an evening, nothing after.
turns.pulledBy: no office term and no sponsored bill dated after the entry
turns.writesBack: the entry reads as it did before, with no looking-back line

turns.what: The writer holds office but brings bills on a different subject than the one the entry was about.
turns.pulledBy: a later term with later bills on another policy area
turns.writesBack: the entry names the office and the later subject, and does not claim the evening's question was taken up
